brief: Goldman's Pasquariello frames the US equity market through three factors: earnings growth, money flow, and the AI narrative. Q2 EPS growth hit 33% and Q3 is tracking 35%, the fastest pace outside post-recession recoveries in 30+ years, but growth is set to slow. If S&P EPS still grows 18% next year, history favors the bulls, though the forecast is highly sensitive to AI capex. Money flow turned negative: hedge funds have been selling non-stop since mid-August, with PB net exposure the lowest since March, households turned net sellers this week, and corporates cut buybacks while large financings cleared the market. He expects flow to improve into year-end but warns 2027 could bring the largest net supply increase since 2000. On AI, consensus sees capex growth slowing from 96% to 44% next year. This week's news is better for hyperscalers but worse for the rest of the AI infrastructure complex, widening the range of outcomes toward more left tails. He concludes the primary uptrend holds for one more push higher, but 2027 looks less rewarding, with volatility set to rise.
